summary: Motion now has three levels (ADR 0028). full is unchanged. reduced removes travel — a Sheet, Drawer or Toast fades in place instead of sliding, a popup starts at its full size instead of growing from 98%, nothing staggers — and stops every keyframe and loop (spinners, Skeleton's pulse, shimmer, ink, sheen, the shader ground, StatusMatrix's clock, smooth scrolling, autoplaying video), while change in place still eases, capped at --ui-duration-base. off collapses every duration to 1ms, as before. WHAT CHANGES FOR USERS: prefers-reduced-motion: reduce now gives reduced, not off, so people with the OS setting see short fades and in-place easing where they saw none; slides, scale-ins and loops stay gone for them. HOW AN APP USES IT: data-ui-motion="full|reduced|off" on any element sets its subtree. reduced and off always win, however attributes nest; full overrides the OS preference and must be set only from a choice the user made in the app (an app motion setting is one attribute on <html>). UNDER THE HOOD: new fixed tokens --ui-motion-level, --ui-motion-travel and --ui-enter-scale, set per level and kept off nested brand scopes; the 14 scale-98 literals and every Sheet, Drawer and Toast offset read them, and Drawer and Toast gain an entry opacity equal to the travel factor, which is 1 at full; the theme redefines Tailwind's motion-safe: and motion-reduce: variants to read the level, so existing guards follow it unchanged; lib/motion gains motionLevel(element) and subscribeMotionLevel(notify), which replace eight direct matchMedia calls. check:motion now refuses a direct prefers-reduced-motion query and a literal scale or slide on an entering or leaving surface; check:fx accepts only @variant motion-safe as a keyframe guard. Storybook has a Motion toolbar switch.

migration.manual: Nothing to rename. Review three things: (1) your own JavaScript that checks matchMedia('(prefers-reduced-motion: reduce)') — switch it to motionLevel(element) from @/lib/motion so it follows the app's setting; (2) your own CSS that slides or scales a surface in by a literal amount — write it against --ui-motion-travel / --ui-enter-scale if it should calm down at reduced; (3) the effects stylesheet must be imported through Tailwind (it now uses @variant motion-safe), not served as a plain <link>. To offer users a motion setting, set data-ui-motion on <html> from their stored choice before first paint.
